evals.prompt: Audit the structure of this Python project that adopted our Clean Architecture + DDD template. Tell me whether it complies.
expected_behaviors: Runs scripts/check_structure.py against the project root before drawing conclusions.
Uses the deterministic script output for directory existence, import, and framework checks.
Does not rely on manual inspection alone for mechanical checks the script covers.
Interprets warnings versus errors correctly: extra directories are warnings, missing required directories are errors.
Reads flagged files and applies references/checklist-ddd.md for issues static analysis cannot detect.
failure_signals: Judges compliance purely by reading the tree without running the checker.
Treats an extra directory (outside the schema) as a hard error.
Treats a missing required directory as a mere warning.
Skips the DDD checklist when reviewing more than folder structure.
Invents a large number of errors when the project uses a different convention instead of adapting the spec.

evals.prompt: I need to add: (a) a business rule that an Order cannot be modified after shipment, (b) an HTTP endpoint to submit an order, (c) a client for an external shipping API, and (d) the dependency wiring. Where does each go in a project using this template?
expected_behaviors: Places the shipment invariant on the Order entity in domain/entities/, pure Python with no frameworks.
Places the HTTP endpoint in infra/controllers/<module>/, kept thin (validate, call use case, format response).
Places the shipping API client in infra/adapters/, implementing an interface from domain/interfaces/adapters/.
Places the wiring in infra/di/, the only place that knows all concrete implementations.
States each choice briefly and proceeds without over-asking.
failure_signals: Puts the business rule in a controller or use case instead of the entity.
Puts the external API client in the domain or application layer as a concrete class.
Instantiates adapters/use cases directly in a controller instead of via di/.
Scatters dependency wiring across multiple modules.
Cannot map the items to layers and guesses.

evals.prompt: The checker reports: `app/src/domain/entities/order.py:3` imports `src.infra.adapters.shipping`. Explain the problem and the fix.
expected_behaviors: States that the domain must not depend on infrastructure (dependency rule points inward).
Explains the fix: define the contract in domain/interfaces/adapters/ and inject the infra implementation through infra/di/.
Notes that this keeps the domain testable without external services and replaceable.
Identifies this as an error, not a warning.
Proposes the plan and waits for confirmation before moving files.
failure_signals: Says it is acceptable for the domain to import infrastructure.
Suggests fixing it by moving the entity into infra/ rather than inverting the dependency.
Treats a domain-to-infra import as a minor style issue.
Moves or deletes files without being asked.
Cannot explain why the dependency rule exists.

evals.prompt: Review this entity: `class Order` has only attributes and getters/setters; all rules (validation, total calculation, status transitions) live in `OrderService` and the controller. Is this a problem under our convention?
expected_behaviors: Identifies an anemic entity: rules scattered across services/controllers belong in the entity.
Recommends moving invariants and behavior onto the Order entity so invalid state is impossible to reach.
Notes that DTOs must not contain business rules and entities must protect invariants.
Uses the DDD checklist reasoning, not just the structural checker, for this judgment.
Recommends ubiquitous language in method names (e.g., approve, ship) over technical terms.
failure_signals: Says an anemic entity with rules in services is fine.
Leaves business rules in the controller.
Relies only on the structural script and misses the modeling issue.
Suggests adding more getters/setters instead of behavior methods.
Cannot distinguish a DTO from an entity.

evals.prompt: Our project is a Backend for Frontend and uses the `bff/` package instead of `src/`. How do I run the structure check?
expected_behaviors: Runs the checker with --package-name bff.
Explains that bff/ keeps the same layers and subdirectories as src/.
Notes that src/ is the default for regular services and bff/ is reserved for BFFs.
Does not report the bff/ package itself as a schema violation.
Mentions --json/--strict options when relevant for CI.
failure_signals: Runs the checker with the default src/ package and reports everything missing.
Claims bff/ is not supported.
Treats the bff/ directory as an error rather than a supported variant.
Is unaware of the --package-name flag.
Invents errors instead of adapting the run to the BFF layout.
